title: Phase Mediator: latency-budgeted tenant interleaving with soft-fairness
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Problem: Current prefill/decode arbitration either prioritizes strict tenant fairness (leading to high P99 tail latency under bursty workloads) or aggressively maximizes throughput (causing priority inversion for latency-sensitive tenants). We need a middle-ground scheduling primitive that enforces tenant latency budgets while preserving proportional fairness over longer windows and allowing kernel selection feedback to influence splitting decisions.

Goal: Design and implement a 'Phase Mediator'—a light-weight runtime component that: 1) maintains per-tenant latency budgets (soft SLOs) across prefill and decode phases, 2) uses a tokenized soft-fairness allocator to interleave micro-slices when budgets are exhausted, 3) emits kernel-hint signals (expected attention cost and execution kernel preference) to the micro-splitter so slices are co-located with compatible kernels, and 4) supports graceful demotion to throughput-optimized paths when the cluster is saturated.

Acceptance criteria:
- New mediator reduces latency SLO violations (P99) for high-priority tenants by >=30% in mixed workloads compared to current baseline scheduler in staging.
- Overall throughput decreases by <5% for representative batch mixes.
- Integrates with existing kernel-probing signals and does not require changes to model artifacts.
- Configuration knobs exposed in Console: per-tenant latency_budget_ms, soft_fair_window_s, demotion_threshold, kernel_hint_weight.

Proposed approach:
1) Latency budget accounting: per-request budget consumption based on estimated remaining decode tokens and an attention-cost estimator (heuristic from recent telemetry). Budgets age out and replenish on a sliding window (soft_fair_window).
2) Tokenized soft-fairness allocator: when multiple ready slices contend, mediator assigns tokens representing budget-weighted entitlement and allows opportunistic interleaving of micro-slices when a tenant's token pool is low. This enables short hedged prefills without starving others.
3) Kernel-hint feedback loop: scheduler consumes kernel preference metadata (e.g., prefers fp16 fused kernel vs quantized kernel) and groups slices to reduce kernel-switch overhead while respecting latency budgets. Kernel hint influence is tunable; default weight is conservative.
4) Burst demotion policy: when cluster-wide queueing or GPU utilization crosses demotion_threshold, the mediator gradually slides lower-priority tenants into throughput path (larger batches, longer queueing) while maintaining tail protections for latency-tiered tenants.

Instrumentation & metrics:
- per-tenant latency_budget_remaining_ms (gauge)
- mediator_allocations{tenant,phase,demoted} (counter)
- kernel_hint_match_ratio (ratio)
- p99_latency_by_tenant_phase (histogram)
- throughput_loss_estimate (gauge)

Tradeoffs and open questions:
- Estimation accuracy: attention-cost estimator errors may misconsume budgets; need fallback conservative multiplier.
- Kernel grouping vs latency: grouping improves kernel efficiency but can increase head-of-line wait for some slices. We expose kernel_hint_weight to tune.
- Complexity: mediator adds state per-tenant; must bound memory and ensure fast path for common-case single-tenant GPUs.

Implementation plan (phases):
A. Prototype mediator in alpha runtime flag; synthetic load tests + staged A/B experiments in canary pool (2 weeks).
B. Integrate kernel-hint ingestion from model-adapter layer + unit tests (1 week).
C. Load test across mixed-tenancy scenarios, tune parameters, collect SLO matrices (2 weeks).
D. Console controls and rollout (1 week).

Rollout: start with non-critical tenants enabled via flag, then ramp to medium customers before enabling for high-value customers. Document knobs and recommended defaults in runbook.
